================================================================
SELJUK — SEQUENCE OF PLAY REFERENCE
================================================================
Source: Rules of Play sections 2.0-4.7 and Player Aid Card,
cross-checked against Seljuk_Errata_and_Clarifications.txt.
Errata corrections applied inline.
 
PRECEDENCE
  Where this file and the Rules of Play or the Errata &
  Clarifications differ, the Rules and the Errata govern.
 
CONVENTIONS
  Player order is Seljuk first, then Roman, unless stated
  otherwise (2.2.4).
  "Turn" = one Seasonal Turn (90 days / one Calendar box).
  Each Turn consists of one Levy sequence followed by one
  Campaign sequence.
  Winter is a non-campaign interphase conducted after Reset
  in the first three Autumn turns only (Calendar boxes 3, 6, 9).
 
 
================================================================
A. LEVY (3.0)
================================================================
Conduct at the outset of each Seasonal Turn.
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.1  ARTS OF WAR (3.1)
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.1.1  Shuffle (3.1.1)
  Collect and shuffle all unused Arts of War cards into each
  side's Event draw deck. Held Events (3.1.3) and Capabilities
  already in play (3.4.4) are NOT included in the draw deck.
 
A.1.2  First Levy of scenario — Draw Capabilities (3.1.2)
  Seljuk then Roman each draw 2 Arts of War cards and deploy
  them as Capabilities (lower half of card, 1.9.1) at that
  side's map edge or Lord mats (1.5.2).
  Return to deck any "This Lord" card that cannot be assigned
  to a Mustered Lord (3.4.4).
 
A.1.3  Second or later Levy — Draw Events (3.1.3)
  Seljuk then Roman each draw 2 Arts of War cards and
  implement their Events (upper half) in the order drawn.
  Reveal Events immediately unless card text says otherwise.
  Event subtypes:
    - Normal Events: resolve immediately, return card to deck.
    - "Hold" Events: keep hidden for later use (e.g., in Battle).
    - "This Campaign" Events: remain in effect until end of
      current Campaign (do not return until Reset, 4.7.5).
      NOTE: The Capability on a "This Campaign" Event card
      is not available for selection this Levy.
    - Asterisk (*) Events: once per game. Mark the current
      Season on the Calendar with the reminder marker.
  NOTE: A side's Events can affect the opposing side. The
  side playing the Event makes any decisions unless otherwise
  specified.
 
A.1.4  Greed (3.1.4)
  Players may not voluntarily discard cards unless permitted
  by a rule. Hold Events return to deck only when used or
  discarded at Campaign's end (4.7.5).
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.2  PAY (3.2)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Seljuk then Roman may expend Coin and Loot to shift Service
Markers right (later) on the Calendar. Coin and Loot may only
be removed in this step to shift Service Markers (1.7.2).
 
A.2.1  Pay with Coin (3.2.1)
  Any Lord with Coin on his mat may remove some or all Coin
  to shift Service Markers right by one Calendar box per Coin:
    - The paying Lord's own Service Marker, OR
    - That of another Lord at the same Locale.
  EXCEPTION: Unbesieged Commanders in play may pay Coin
  regardless of location for any Unbesieged friendly Lord.
 
A.2.2  Pay with Loot (3.2.2)
  Any Lord at a Friendly Locale free of Siege (may be
  Bypassed) may pay with Loot from his mat (or Share from
  a Lord at the same Locale) as if Coin, one for one.
  IMPORTANT: Must be at a Friendly Locale free of Siege.
  May do so at an Unbesieged Stronghold with that side's
  Conquered markers, but NOT at a Besieged Locale.
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.3  DISBAND (3.3)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Seljuk then Roman check for Lord Disbanding.
 
A.3.1  Beyond Service Limit (3.3.1)
  For each Lord whose Service Marker is to the LEFT of the
  current Levy/Campaign marker (in a lower-numbered Turn
  box), remove him from the map.
  REMOVAL: Permanently remove cylinder(s) from play. Set
  aside mat, Service Marker, Vassal Service Markers, Forces,
  and Assets. Return "This Lord" Capability cards (3.4.4) to
  the Arts of War deck.
  If the Lord was Seljuk and had a Roman Strategic Objective
  marker, the Roman player claims it in the Constantinople
  Holding Box.
 
A.3.2  At Service Limit (3.3.2)
  Lords with Service Markers in the SAME Turn box as the
  Levy/Campaign marker Disband but may Muster again later.
  - Place cylinder on the Calendar, a number of Seasonal Turn
    boxes to the RIGHT equal to the Lord's Service Rating
    (1.5.3). If beyond box 12, place off the board (2.2.3).
  - Return Forces and Assets to pools. Return Capability cards
    under the mat to the Arts of War deck. Set aside mat(s),
    Service Marker, and remaining Vassal Service Markers.
  CLARIFICATION (Errata): If the Roman Commander Disbands
  while Themata Service Markers are on his Lord mat, those
  Themata are returned to their Thema box.
  NOTE: Rarely, a Lord may Disband because his last unit is
  removed outside of combat (1.6).
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.4  MUSTER (3.4)
----------------------------------------------------------------
After Disband, Seljuk then Roman Lords already on the map
may take Levy actions up to their Lordship Rating (1.5.3) to
Muster other Lords, Vassals, Transport, or Capabilities.
Each Levy action spends one point of Lordship. Complete each
Lord's actions before the next Lord, in any order desired.
 
REQUIREMENTS: A Lord must have begun this Muster segment
at an Unbesieged Friendly Locale (1.3.1) including a Holding
Box. Lords may NOT conduct Muster from Enemy Locales or
at a Siege. Lords brought onto the map during this Muster
segment (3.4.1) may not take Levy actions themselves until
that Levy's Call to Arms at the earliest (3.5).
 
A.4.1  Levy Other Lords (3.4.1)
  Cost: 1 Lordship per attempt.
  Designate a Lord to roll Fealty for another Lord. The rolling
  Lord must be Ready (cylinder in a Turn box at or left of the
  Levy marker, 2.2) and must have a Seat free of enemy Lords
  or Conquered markers (may be Bypassed or Ravaged, 4.5.5).
  Roll one die; if within the target Lord's Fealty Rating (1.5.3),
  Muster him. If not, do nothing (may retry with more Lordship).
  NOTE: Lords can Levy a Ready Commander like any other Lord.
 
  MUSTERING procedure:
    - Place Lord's cylinder at one of his free Seats (or for
      Arisighi, Robert, or Roussel only, his associated Holding
      Box per 1.4.2 if Seat is enemy-occupied/Conquered).
    - Take Lord's mat; place starting Forces from pool (1.6).
    - Place Assets and Vassal Service Markers (Heraldry up,
      Ready to Muster, 3.4.2) onto Lord's mat. Keep aside any
      Special Vassal Service Markers not yet available (1.5.1,
      1.9.1, 3.4.2).
      NOTE: Do NOT place Vassal Forces on the mat when the
      Lord Musters; they are available for the Lord to Levy at
      a later time.
    - Place Lord's Service Marker on the Calendar, a number
      of boxes to the RIGHT of the current Levy box equal to
      his Service Rating (1.5.3). If beyond 12, place off-board
      (2.2.3).
 
A.4.2  Levy Vassals (3.4.2)
  Cost: 1 Lordship.
  Vassal must have a face-up Service Marker in the Lord's
  Assets & Vassals section. Slide it to Forces section. Place
  the units shown on the marker from the pool (1.6).
  NOTE: Ignore Vassal Service Ratings unless using optional
  rule 6.2.
  SPECIAL VASSALS (Scholai, Emperor's Retinue, Elite Ghulam
  Cavalry, Oghuz Mercenaries): start set aside until the
  associated Capability enables Levy. Discard of the card
  Disbands the Vassal.
 
A.4.3  Levy Transport (3.4.3)
  Cost: 1 Lordship.
  Lord at a Friendly Locale adds one Cart to his mat.
 
A.4.4  Levy Capabilities (3.4.4)
  Cost: 1 Lordship per card selected.
  Lord at a Friendly Locale obtains Capabilities (bottom half
  of Arts of War cards). Select from any of the side's currently
  unused cards, within restrictions:
    - Heraldry shows which Lords can Levy the card and whom
      it affects ("This Lord", "any", "ALL", "NOT").
    - "This Lord" cards: place at bottom edge of that Lord's
      mat. Max two "This Lord" Capabilities per Lord mat, no
      duplicates. Drawing a third forces immediate discard of
      one.
    - "ALL" / non-"This Lord" cards: tuck upper half under
      the player's closest game board edge (2.1.1). A Lord may
      Levy any number of such Capabilities (see also 4.0).
  NOTE: Levying a Capability blocks its Event from occurring.
 
A.4.5  Levy Themata (3.4.5)
  Cost: 1 Lordship (spent by Roman Commander only).
  During Muster, the Roman Commander may Levy Themata
  Service Markers as if performing a Recruit action (4.5.7) in
  his current Thema. Place the marker on the Lord's mat and
  stack the depicted unit(s) on it.
  NOTE: This differs from Vassal handling in this game and
  previous Levy & Campaign volumes.
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
A.5  CALL TO ARMS (3.5)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Each side has different strategic options depending on Levied
Capabilities. Each Call to Arms phase, Seljuks may complete
any one option, then Romans do so.
NOTE: Events can trigger at most one Call to Arms per Levy.
 
A.5.1  Capability-driven options (3.5.1)
  MARWANID ALLIANCE: Seljuk player may transfer 1 Coin
  from Alp Arslan's Assets to this card OR spend any number
  of Coin from the Marwanid Alliance card; for each Coin
  spent, make either Amid or Mayyafariqin a Seat for Seljuk
  Lords until the next Winter Phase. Lords may not Tax in
  these Locales and only one may serve as a Supply Source per
  Command card. Place Lord Seat marker(s) as reminder.
 
  EMPRESS EUDOKIA MAKREMBOLITISSA (3.5.1.2): Roman
  player may either place the Empress token on this card OR
  move it from this card to Constantinople to choose one of:
    - Shift a Roman Lord cylinder 1 Calendar box.
    - Decrease service of a Lord with a Seat at Constantinople
      1 Calendar box to increase service of Romanos Diogenes
      by 1 Calendar box.
 
  DEEP RAIDS: A Lord meeting criteria on the card may
  execute the Call to Arms action for the turn.
 
A.5.2  Loot (3.5.2)
  If desired, Seljuk player may remove a Loot marker from the
  Mosul and Baghdad box (adjusting VPs) to shift a Seljuk Lord
  cylinder 1 Calendar box.
 
A.5.3  Strategic Objective (3.5.3)
  [ERRATA APPLIED — PAC correction]
  If desired, and if a Roman Commander is in Constantinople,
  the Roman player may:
    - Take a Strategic Objective marker from the supply and
      make it available in front of them, OR
    - If they already have one or more available Strategic
      Objective markers in front of them from a previous Call
      to Arms, place one on a Mustered enemy Lord mat or an
      Enemy Stronghold in the Sultanate (1.3.1).
  May NOT take from supply AND place in the same Call to
  Arms. Three markers exist; Roman player may hold all three.
  Once claimed for VPs (3.3.1, 4.5.1, 4.9.1), the marker goes
  permanently to the Constantinople Holding Box.
 
 
================================================================
B. CAMPAIGN (4.0)
================================================================
After Levy, conduct the Turn's Seasonal Campaign.
 
CAPABILITY DISCARD: Players (Seljuk first) must select and
discard any Capability cards they have exceeding their number
of Mustered Lords — not counting "This Lord" Capabilities
(3.4.4). Compare the number of non-"This Lord" cards under
a side's map edge to its number of Lord mats in use; discard
any excess.
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
B.1  PLAN (4.1)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Each side builds a Campaign Plan: an ordered stack of Command
cards (1.9.2). May designate Lieutenants (4.1.3).
 
B.1.1  Selecting Cards (4.1.1)
  Use any cards available in that side's Command deck. Action
  cards (with a numeral) and No Command cards always
  available.
  Plan stack size by Season:
    - Spring: 7 cards
    - Summer: 8 cards
    - Autumn: 7 cards
  NOTE: Some Events may add more cards.
 
B.1.2  Arranging Stacks (4.1.2)
  Stack the required number of cards face down in any order.
  Top face-down card = first Active Lord. May not rearrange
  once built. Players may always inspect their own Plan and
  the other side's played (but not unused) Command cards.
 
B.1.3  Lieutenants (4.1.3)
  During Planning only, players may stack a Lord cylinder atop
  another at the same Locale. Upper = Lieutenant, Lower =
  Lower Lord. Lieutenant oversees Lower Lord for entire
  Campaign unless one is removed. Max one Lower Lord per
  Lieutenant. Lower Lord may not be a Lieutenant. Commanders
  may not be Lieutenants or Lower Lords. A side may have
  several Lieutenants.
  Lieutenant and Lower Lord always move together (March,
  Avoid, Retreat, etc.).
  If either Disbands, the remaining Lord becomes a normal Lord.
  Revealing a Lower Lord's Command card results in a Pass.
  A Lieutenant and Lower Lord may not Withdraw into a Fort
  (Size 1).
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
B.2  COMMAND (4.2)
----------------------------------------------------------------
After building Plan stacks, Seljuk then Roman alternate
flipping (revealing) the top Command card — one Seljuk, then
one Roman, and so on.
 
B.2.1  Actions (4.2.1)
  Lord on a revealed Command card may execute a series of
  Commands up to his Command Rating (1.5.3), in any order.
  EXCEPTIONS: Besieged Lords (4.3.5) may only Sally (4.5.3),
  Pass (4.5.8), or perhaps Forage (4.5.4). Siege and Tax use
  an entire card (4.5.1, 4.5.6). Starting a Siege and any Battle
  or Storm end that card's actions (4.3.5, 4.8, 4.9).
  NOTE: Lords may use multiple actions on a single Command
  type (e.g., Forage three times).
 
B.2.2  Command Menu (4.2.2)
  Available Commands: March, Siege, Storm, Sally, Supply,
  Forage, Ravage, Tax, or Pass. Romans can Recruit (4.5.7).
 
B.2.3  No Command Card (4.2.3)
  Revealed No Command card, a Lower Lord's card (4.1.3), or
  the card of a Lord not on the map: that side does nothing.
  Play passes to the other side, or ends the Campaign if
  neither side has cards left in its Plan (4.7).
 
  NOTE: After each Command card, Lords who moved and/or
  fought will Feed their Forces, and Lords may Pay or might
  Disband (4.6).
 
  [COMMANDS 4.3-4.5 — March, Supply, Siege, Storm, Sally,
  Forage, Ravage, Tax, Recruit, Pass — are detailed in the
  Rules of Play sections 4.3 through 4.5.8. See also the
  Commands side of the Player Aid Card.]
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
B.3  FEED — PAY — DISBAND (4.6)
----------------------------------------------------------------
At the end of EACH Command card, both sides execute:
 
B.3.1  Feed (4.6.1)
  Each Lord who Moved or Fought (Seljuk then Roman) must
  remove Provender or Loot per the number of units on his mat:
    - 1-8 units: 1 Provender or Loot
    - 9-12 units: 2
    - 13-16 units: 3
    - 17+ units: 4
  GREED: Feed may not remove Assets beyond this requirement
  (1.7.2). NOTE: Loot Pays Lords only at Friendly Locales
  (3.2.2) but Feeds them anywhere.
  SHARING: All Lords at a Locale must first Feed their own
  Forces from their own mats. Then Lords must expend
  Provender and Loot to Feed co-located Friendly Lords who
  did not fully Feed. A side may not withhold.
 
  UNFED: Shift Service Marker left one Seasonal box for each
  Lord that received less Provender or Loot than required.
  (If using Vassal Service optional rule 6.2, also shift Vassals.)
  A Lord requiring 2 or 3 but with access to fewer consumes
  them and still suffers the shift.
 
B.3.2  Pay and Disband (4.6.2)
  Any Seljuk then Roman Lords may receive Pay as per Levy
  (3.2). Then all Lords on both sides Disband as required by
  their Service limit (3.3.1-.2).
 
B.3.3  Remove Markers (4.6.3)
  Remove Moved/Fought markers from all Lords. Proceed with
  the other side's next Command card, if any.
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
B.4  END CAMPAIGN (4.7)
----------------------------------------------------------------
After revealing all Command cards in both sides' Plan stacks,
end this Seasonal Turn.
 
B.4.1  Game End (4.7.1)
  If this was the scenario's final Seasonal Turn, the game ends.
  Side with the most VPs wins (5.3). If tied, draw.
 
B.4.2  Grow (4.7.2)
  At the end of each SPRING Turn (Calendar boxes 1, 4, 7, 10):
  Seljuk then Roman each must select and reduce the Enemy's
  Ravaged markers on the map to half their total number,
  rounded up (adjust VPs, 5.1).
 
B.4.3  Repair (4.7.3)
  At the end of each Campaign: remove one Siege marker from
  each Stronghold that has three or four Siege markers.
 
B.4.4  Wastage (4.7.4)
  Seljuks then Romans must select and discard any one Asset
  or "This Lord" Capability card from each Lord who has more
  than one of any type of Asset or more than one such card.
 
B.4.5  Reset (4.7.5)
  Prepare for the next Turn:
    - Roman Commander may retain Themata Service Markers
      and their units from a Thema on his mat by paying 1 Coin
      per Thema with units present. If not, return each unpaid
      Themata marker to its home Thema and remove the
      provided Forces (1.6).
    - Unstack any Lieutenants and Lower Lords (4.1.3).
    - Discard all "This Campaign" Events (3.1.3).
    - Seljuk then Roman player may discard any Arts of War
      cards back into their decks (1.9.1).
    - Advance Campaign marker to the next Seasonal Turn box
      and flip the marker to Levy (2.2.2).
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
B.5  WINTER (4.7.6)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Conduct this phase after Reset in the first three AUTUMN turns
only (Calendar boxes 3, 6, and 9).
 
B.5.1  Aleppo Independence Victory Check
  If the ALEPPO INDEPENDENCE event has been played for its
  effect AND Aleppo is Seljuk Conquered, the Seljuk player
  wins an automatic victory (5.2).
 
B.5.2  Bounty
  [ERRATA APPLIED — page 18, 4.7.6]
  A Seljuk Lord who can trace a path of Locales that are
  Ruins, Wilderness, Unfortified Settlements, Friendly
  Strongholds free of enemy Lords, or Bypassed or Besieged
  Enemy Strongholds back to his Seat may score 1 VP per Loot
  on his Lord mat up to the number of Carts he and co-located
  Lords currently possess.
  Carts do not need to be assigned to a Way; their number just
  limits the amount of Loot that can be scored.
  Scored Loot tokens go into the Mosul & Baghdad Holding Box
  to track those VPs.
 
B.5.3  Seljuk Unity
  Count total Locales with Seljuk-colored Ruins, Conquered,
  or Ravaged markers (not VP value) on the map. Compare to
  the yearly Seljuk Unity value on the Calendar (Autumn box).
  If the number of Locales with those markers is LESS than the
  Calendar value, the Seljuk player loses VPs equal to the
  difference, removing Loot in Mosul & Baghdad first (if any),
  then placing Roman Conquered 1 VP markers in the
  Constantinople Holding Box. These Roman Conquered 1 VP
  markers are removed first when the Seljuk player scores
  positive VPs during a future Bounty phase.
 
B.5.4  Winter Quarters
  Unless allowed by a Capability to ignore this phase, return
  all Lords to their Seats Unladen by discarding any excess
  Assets (1.7.2). If a Lord's Seat is Enemy Conquered, place
  Lord in their Allied Holding Box. Each Lord then reduces
  his Carts to half their number, rounded up.
  Remove any MARWANID ALLIANCE Seat markers from map.
 
B.5.5  Aleppo Diplomacy
  If the Independent Aleppo marker is currently on the map,
  roll a die. On 1-2, remove the marker. On 3-6, it remains.
 
 
================================================================
C. VICTORY (5.0)
================================================================
C.1  Earning Victory Points (5.1)
  Track VPs on the Calendar (2.2.5).
    - Each side earns 1/2 VP per Ruins marker of its color.
    - Each side earns 1/2 VP per Ravaged marker of its color.
    - Roman player earns 1 VP per Roman Conquered marker
      on the map.
  Add to each side's total:
    - Roman: 1 VP each for Strategic Objective markers and
      Conquered markers in the Constantinople Holding Box.
    - Seljuk: 1 VP each for Loot markers in the Mosul &
      Baghdad Holding Box.
 
C.2  Campaign Victory (5.2)
  If at any moment during Campaign a side has NO Mustered
  Lords on the map, the game ends immediately — the other
  side wins regardless of VPs.
  The Seljuk player wins in the first phase of Winter if they
  have Conquered Aleppo and the ALEPPO INDEPENDENCE Event
  has been played for its effect.
 
C.3  End of Scenario Victory (5.3)
  If neither side wins by the Game End step (4.7.1) of the last
  Campaign, the side with more VPs wins. If tied, draw.

# SELJUK - UNITS AND STRONGHOLDS REFERENCE (YAML)
# ============================================================
# Source: Player Aid Card (Forces / Strongholds), cross-checked
# against Seljuk_Rules.pdf, Seljuk_Background_Book_web.pdf, and
# Seljuk_Errata_and_Clarifications.txt.
#
# Omitted from source: "Piece" column (visual only), die color
# (visual mnemonic only; all rolls use standard d6).
# Errata corrections applied inline; original printed text noted
# where it differs.
# ============================================================

metadata:
  game: Seljuk
  document_type: units_and_strongholds_reference
  source_card: Forces / Strongholds player aid
  dice: All rolls use standard d6
  conventions:
    strike_value: "Number of dice rolled per unit (e.g., 1 = x1, 0.5 = x1/2). Sum within a step, round up."
    protection_range: "Roll within range cancels the Hit; outside the range, the unit Routs."
    any_1_round: "Strike usable in exactly one Round of a Battle, player's choice."
    mark: "Once-per-Battle effect; track with a marker."
    asterisks: "On the player aid card, asterisks link strike/protection values to capability-modifier notes."

# ============================================================
# FORCES
# ============================================================

forces:

  # ---------- HORSE ----------

  tagmata:
    category: horse
    allegiance: Roman
    strikes:
      missile: 0.5
      melee:
        value: 1
        capability_modifier: BARDOUKIA
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 3]
        capability_modifier: KLIBANOPHOROI
    capabilities:
      BARDOUKIA:
        scope: melee
        effect: "-1 to target Armor during Melee"
        clarification_R21: "Roll Protection against Bardoukia Hits separately from other Hits in the same Melee step."
      KLIBANOPHOROI:
        scope: armor
        effect: "Armor range becomes 1-4"

  norman_knights:
    category: horse
    allegiance: Roman
    strikes:
      melee: 2
      storm: 1
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 4]
        capability_modifier: NORMAN_HEAVY_CAVALRY
    capabilities:
      NORMAN_HEAVY_CAVALRY:
        scope: armor
        effect: "Re-roll 1 unit Armor each Missiles and Melee"

  scholai_hetaireia:
    category: horse
    allegiance: Roman
    strikes:
      missile: 1
      melee: 1
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 4]
    capabilities: {}

  ghulam_cavalry:
    category: horse
    allegiance: Seljuk
    strikes:
      missile: 0.5
      melee: 1
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 4]
    capabilities: {}

  turkic_horse:
    category: horse
    allegiance: Seljuk
    strikes:
      missile:
        value: 1
        capability_modifier: PARTHIAN_SHOT
      melee:
        value: 0.5
        capability_modifier: SHOCK_TACTICS
    protection:
      unarmored:
        range: [1, 1]
        applies_to: "Missile Hits, and any Hits in Storm"
      evade:
        range: [1, 3]
        applies_to: "Melee Hits in Battle only (not Missiles, not Storm)"
      armored:
        range: [1, 3]
        capability_modifier: LAMELLAR_ARMOR
        note: "Armored protection requires LAMELLAR_ARMOR capability; not available by default"
    capabilities:
      PARTHIAN_SHOT:
        scope: missile
        effect: "Select Missile targets (like Garrison Archers)"
      SHOCK_TACTICS:
        scope: melee
        printed_text: "x1/2 Melee in Battle/Storm (round up)"
        errata_clarification_playbook_p14: |
          Half (rounded up) of the Lord's Turkic Horse do x1/2 Melee
          Hits each. Example: 3 Turkic Horse → 2 units (3 x 0.5
          rounded up) do x1/2 Hit each = 1 Hit total.
      LAMELLAR_ARMOR:
        scope: armor
        printed_text: "Armor 1-3 until 3 Rout"
        available_to: [Emir of Arran, Alp Arslan, Artuk Beg]
        S1_S2_clarification: |
          Capability stops applying for the remainder of the Battle
          immediately upon 3 Turkic Horse units Routing from this
          Lord. If Lord has fewer than 3 Turkic Horse, capability
          always applies.
        errata_clarification_p17: |
          On a Melee Hit, the player may choose EITHER Lamellar Armor
          (1-3) OR Evade (1-3) for the Protection roll, per Hit.
          The two do not stack.
    special_rules_if_all_turkic_horse:
      first_march_command_cost_modifier: -1
      pursuit_exception: "If single Seljuk Lord (with only Turkic Horse) Concedes to single Roman Lord, BOTH sides have Hits halved in Pursuit."

  # ---------- FOOT ----------

  varangian_guard:
    category: foot
    allegiance: Roman
    strikes:
      melee:
        value: 3
        restriction: "May Strike in first Round only, no halving for Pursuit (mark)"
        errata_correction: "Printed card reads 'May attack in Melee in first Round only'; Errata corrects 'attack in Melee' to 'Strike'."
      storm: 1
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 4]
    capabilities: {}

  infantry:
    category: foot
    allegiance: both
    strikes:
      missile:
        value: 1
        availability: any_1_round
        requires_capability: JAVELINS
        depicted_with_javelins_icon: true
      melee: 1
    protection:
      armored:
        range: [1, 3]
        capability_modifier: STEELED_RESOLVE
    storm_garrison_property:
      missile_rate_when_garrison: 0.5
      target_armor_modifier: -1
      select_target: true
      rule_reference: 4.9.1
      note: "Infantry in a Stronghold Garrison during Storm gains x1/2 Missile strikes even without Javelins capability."
    capabilities:
      JAVELINS:
        scope: missile
        effect: "Any 1 Round: x1 Missiles in Battle"
      ALAKATIA:
        scope: missile
        effect: "2 Infantry in Battle add 1 extra Missile Hit with -1 to target Armor"
        clarification_R23: |
          Requires at least 2 Unrouted Infantry under this Lord to
          trigger. Effect does not scale with more than 2 Infantry
          (e.g., 4 Infantry does not generate 2 extra Hits). If
          subsequent Rounds bring the Lord below 2 Unrouted
          Infantry, the extra Hit is not generated. Defender should
          roll Protection against the Alakatia Hit separately, since
          it has the same anti-armor effect as Garrison Missiles.
      STEELED_RESOLVE:
        scope: armor
        effect: "Armor 1-4 vs Horse 1 Round (mark)"

  militia:
    category: foot
    allegiance: both
    strikes:
      missile:
        value: 0.5
        capability_modifier: PSILOI
      melee: 0.5
    protection:
      unarmored:
        range: [1, 1]
        capability_modifier: SYNDOSIS
    capabilities:
      PSILOI:
        scope: missile
        effect: "Missiles x1/2"
        scope_R25: |
          Applies to all non-garrison Roman Militia in play. Roman
          Garrison Militia already have Missile x1/2 with -1 to
          target Armor by default (4.9.1).
        placement: "Board edge (Lord ALL); not attached to any Lord."
      SYNDOSIS:
        scope: armor
        effect: "Armor 1-2"

# ============================================================
# STRONGHOLDS
# ============================================================

strongholds:

  city:
    value: 3
    size_symbol: 3
    capacity_lords_to_add_siege: 3
    walls_range: [1, 4]
    surrender_dice: 3
    has_gardens: true
    icon_description: "Tree + large multi-building walls"
    garrison_roman:
      spawned_units: {infantry: 1, militia: 1}
      garrison_archers: &garrison_archers
        missile: 0.5
        target_armor_modifier: -1
        select_target: true
      themata_optional:
        max_depicted_on_aid: 3
        source: "Local Thema box on map"
        chosen_by: Roman player at start of Siege

================================================================
SELJUK - THEMATA SCENARIO REFERENCE
================================================================
 
Combines the master Themata Service Marker roster (from the
user's physical-counter inventory, cross-checked against the
rulebook) with the per-scenario "Remove from Play" lists and
face-up map placements for all five published scenarios.
 
SOURCES
  - Master roster: user-provided marker inventory (May 2026).
  - Removal lists, Calendar data, face-up placements: rulebook
    scenario pages 26-35 and the printed scenario-setup map
    illustrations.
  - Cross-checks: rulebook "Remove from Play" text, playbook
    examples, project Map Reference.
 
PRECEDENCE
  Where this file and the Rules of Play or the Errata &
  Clarifications differ, the Rules and the Errata govern.
 
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
MARKER NOTATION
----------------------------------------------------------------
 
Each line in a Thema's roster is ONE Themata Service Marker.
 
  "1 Infantry"     single-symbol Infantry marker
  "2 Infantry"     one marker depicting 2 Infantry symbols
                   ("double infantry" in scenario text). Rolls
                   one Protection die for Ravage and is Lost on
                   a failed roll; deploys 2 Infantry units as
                   Garrison in Storm. (Rules 1.5.1)
  "1 Tagmata"      single-symbol Tagmata marker
  "1 Militia"      single-symbol Militia marker
  "1 Turkic Horse" single-symbol Turkic Horse marker
 
Themata are Roman-side only. They are placed in their Thema box
on the map at setup, and both players may inspect a Thema box's
contents at any time -- there is no face-down / hidden state for
markers sitting in their home box (Rules 1.5.1). The counter
back simply shows the Thema name as a placement reminder.
 
"Face-up on the map" in the scenario sections below refers to a
marker the scenario-setup illustration shows displayed at a
specific Stronghold Locale rather than tucked in the Thema box.
This is a setup/visual convention; rules-wise the marker still
belongs to its Thema.
 
Paphlagonia is omitted from all rosters: its only Locale is the
Constantinople Holding Box, and no scenario references a
Paphlagonia Themata marker.
 
 
----------------------------------------------------------------
VERIFICATION STATUS KEY
----------------------------------------------------------------
 
  [rulebook]   The marker is named explicitly in rulebook
               scenario "Remove from Play" text, so its
               existence and type are confirmed.
  [inventory]  The marker comes from the user's physical-counter
               reading. No scenario thins this marker, so the
               rulebook offers no cross-check. Treated as accurate.
 
  The full roster below is treated as accurate. Themata Garrison
  markers are drawn only from Infantry, double Infantry, Tagmata,
  Militia, and Turkic Horse types; Scholai/Hetaireia and Norman
  Knights are Lord Forces and Vassal units, never Themata, so
  they would not appear in a Thema box. Turkic Horse is the only
  mounted Themata type (confirmed at Iberia), which settles the
  Melitene mounted marker as a Turkic Horse.
 
 
================================================================
MASTER ROSTER -- 1068 BASELINE
================================================================
This is the full set of Themata Service Markers before any
scenario removals. "The Emperor and the Lion" (1068) uses this
roster minus only its own removal (see that scenario below).

[Note: The source document uses red text to denote corrections and green text to denote clarifications. Strikethrough text indicates content to be removed. This plain-text version marks those with explicit annotations: [STRIKETHROUGH: ...] for removed text. Corrected/added text in the original red is preserved inline within the quoted passages.]

ERRATA

    "*May Strike in first Round only, no halving for Pursuit (mark)."

    "Before the next Pay phase (Autumn 1070), the Roman player places Robert's cylinder at his Seat in Edessa."
 
 
Page 18 (4.7.6 Winter, Bounty segment) - corrections in red. Enemy Lords block the Bounty path trace.
 
    "Bounty. A Seljuk Lord who can trace a path of Locales that are either Ruins, Wilderness, Unfortified Settlements, Friendly Strongholds free of enemy Lords, or Bypassed or Besieged Enemy Strongholds back to his Seat may score 1 VP per Loot on his Lord mat up to the number of Carts he and co-located Lords currently possess."
 
 
Page 34 (1071 A.D. scenario Roman setup, second bullet) - corrections in red. PSILOI is an ALL Capability and should start under the board edge, not attached to Andronikos Doukas.
 
    "Andronikos Doukas at CONSTANTINOPLE (with 2 Carts in Assets on Lord Mat and [STRIKETHROUGH: PSILOI and] SYNDOSIS Capability Levied)"

----------------------------------------------------------------
PLAYBOOK
----------------------------------------------------------------
 
Page 14 (Example of Play, 2nd and 3rd paragraph) - corrections in red. SHOCK TACTICS ability should make half Alp Arslan's horse units (3 x 0.5 rounded = 2) do 1/2 Hit, for a total of 1 Hit.
 
    "The Seljuk player then counts up his hits: half (rounded up) of Alp Arslan's Turkic Horse have x1/2 Hits due to Shock Tactics, which is x1 in total (after rounding), along with x1 for the remaining Ghulam.
 
    The Roman player rolls Walls and gets a 1, 4 to cancel both hits before they get to his lone defending Tagmata unit."
 
 
Page 17 (Example of Play: Battle - Retreat/Withdraw/Ruin) - corrections in red. As the attacker, the Roman player cannot Withdraw into Theodosiopolis (the site of Battle) because they are neither the defender nor Sallying. They must retreat back to Keltzene.
 
    "The Romans must retreat back to Keltzene from where the attack was launched [STRIKETHROUGH: or they could choose to Withdraw inside Theodosiopolis, since it is Roman Friendly]."
 
    [Resulting corrected text: "The Romans must retreat back to Keltzene from where the attack was launched."]
 
 
================================================================
CLARIFICATIONS
================================================================
 
Page 17 (Example of Play, 3rd paragraph) - clarification in green. The Seljuk player can use either LAMELLAR ARMOR or Evade for his Protection value since this is a melee strike.
 
    "The next roll is a 2, which nullifies the Hit (thanks to LAMELLAR ARMOR or, since this is a melee strike, Evade)."
 
 
What happens to Themata on the Roman Commander's Lord Mat if he disbands?
 
    They are returned to their Thema box.

# Rules Decisions

Adjudicated rules calls. Each entry records the user's verbatim answer, the
rules citation (or [HOUSE RULE] if the rules are silent), and the commit hash
where the decision is encoded. **Decisions are permanent — never delete an
entry.** When the user answers a question in `RULES_QUESTIONS.md`, MOVE it here.

Format per entry:
- **D-NNN** (matches the originating Q-NNN where applicable)
- **Question** — the question as posed.
- **Decision** — the user's verbatim adjudication.
- **Citation** — rule section, or [HOUSE RULE].
- **Encoded in** — commit hash / file / test.

---

## D-001 (from Q-001) — Way type of the Khliat <-> Anzitene connection

- **Question.** Is the Khliat <-> Anzitene Way a Road or a Pass? The text
  sources do not determine it (the adjacency graph exists only on the printed
  board); the Map Reference listed it as a Pass but flagged that as a guess.
- **Decision.** "Khliat to Anzitene is a pass." (Eric, 2026-05-20, confirming
  from the physical game board.)
- **Citation.** Game board map topology (Rules of Play 1.3.1, Ways). The Map
  Reference's tentative classification is hereby confirmed correct.
- **Encoded in.** To be encoded in `src/seljuk/data/static/map.json` during
  Phase 1, with this decision cited; map-integrity test will assert 15 Pass
  Ways including Khliat <-> Anzitene.


## D-002 (from Q-002) — Turkic Horse have no base Melee; Shock Tactics grants it

- **Question.** Do Turkic Horse have any Melee without the Shock Tactics
  Capability (S4/S6)?
- **Decision (Eric, 2026-05-20).** "Turkic Horse have no base Melee; Shock
  Tactics is what grants them any Melee at all." Model: base Melee = 0; with
  Shock Tactics on the Lord, ceil(n/2) of his Turkic Horse strike at x1/2 in
  Melee (Battle and Storm).
- **Citation.** Playbook p.17 Battle Example of Play is decisive: Alp Arslan has
  Lamellar (not Shock Tactics) and unrouted Turkic Horse, yet in the Defending
  Horse Melee step only his Ghulam produce Hits ("no more Horse units that can
  Melee") — the Turkic Horse produce none. Card text S4 is granting language
  ("Half of this Lord's Turkic Horse HAVE Melee x1/2"); the S4 clarification and
  Playbook p.14 example (3 Turkic -> 2 units x1/2 = 1 Hit) confirm the arithmetic.
- **Encoded in.** battle.py (`_HORSE_MELEE` omits Turkic Horse; Shock Tactics
  adds ceil(n/2)x0.5 in `_lord_step_hits_caps` and `_lord_melee_capped`);
  forces.json turkic_horse Melee rewritten as
  {base:0, granted_by:SHOCK_TACTICS, value_when_granted:0.5, applies_to:ceil(n/2)}.
  Tests: test_phase4b_combat_caps.test_shock_tactics_grants_turkic_melee_s4_q002.


## D-002 (from Q-002) — Steeled Resolve (R3) Infantry armor value

- **Question.** Does R3 Steeled Resolve set the Lord's Infantry armor to 1-3 or
  1-4 vs Horse? The Arts of War Reference said "Armor 1-3" (card text +
  clarification), but the Units data + engine implement base Infantry 1-3 with
  Steeled Resolve -> 1-4; "1-3" would be a no-op.
- **Decision.** "Infantry base armor confirmed at 1-3. ... Steeled Resolve grants
  Armor 1-4 vs. Horse for the marked round." (Eric, 2026-06-09.) Rationale: a
  Capability granting the armor Infantry already have would be a dead card half;
  the pattern of Protection Capabilities is +1-style bumps (Klibanophoroi 1-3->1-4,
  Syndosis Unarmored->1-2); the rulebook's Protection worked example is exactly
  "a '+1' to Armor improves 1-3 to 1-4"; 1-4 is the elite-foot ceiling (Varangian).
- **Citation.** Player Aid Forces table (Infantry base Armor 1-3) + Rules of Play
  Protection section. The Arts of War Reference's "1-3" is a propagated
  transcription error (a single mistranscription echoed into the clarification);
  corrected in that file with a sourcing note. Derived correction, NOT published
  errata -- official Errata, if it ever addresses R3, takes precedence.
- **Encoded in.** Already implemented in `src/seljuk/capabilities.py`
  (`protection_range`: Steeled Resolve vs Horse -> (1,4)) and `battle.py`
  (vs-Horse scope = Missile+Melee in the owner-declared Round, Ruling 2, commit
  60450cf). Reference corrected in `reference/Seljuk Arts of War Reference.txt`.
  Tests: `tests/test_r3_steeled_resolve_and_s24.py`.


## D-006 (from Q-002, 2026-07-05) — Marwanid Alliance Seats (3.5.1.1) allow MUSTER

- **Question.** Do activated Amid/Mayyafariqin count as Seats for Muster
  (3.4.1), or only for Supply Routes / Bounty?
- **Decision.** "Unless we can make the case that muster is prohibited in this
  circumstance, allow it. It would have been easy for the sources to say it was
  not allowed if it weren't." (Eric, 2026-07-06.) Muster at an activated
  Marwanid Seat is ALLOWED for any Seljuk Lord while the activation lasts.
- **Citation.** 3.5.1.1 "a Seat for Seljuk Lords until the end of the next
  Winter Phase" with only the Tax and Supply-Source carve-outs; Lords Reference
  Seats lines ("Amid?, Mayyafariqin?" on every Seljuk Lord). Winter-Quarters
  return remains printed-Seats-only: the Playbook Winter example lists Alp
  Arslan's Quarters options exhaustively (Ani or the Mosul & Baghdad box)
  while Amid is active — a positive case that Quarters is excluded, which the
  no-prohibition principle above therefore does not override.
- **Encoded in.** `actions._muster_seats` (+ the levy_lord per-Seat palette);
  tests `test_decisions_d002m_d003.py::test_marwanid_seat_offered_and_used_for_muster_3511`
  / `..._not_offered_when_inactive_3511`.


## D-007 (from Q-003, 2026-07-05) — Loot / Empress cylinder shifts go EITHER direction

- **Question.** Does "shift a Lord cylinder 1 Calendar box" (3.5.2 Loot,
  3.5.1.2 Empress) permit shifting right (delaying Readiness)?
- **Decision.** "Allow shifting right. If it doesn't just say shift left, when
  it could, it must mean shift either direction." (Eric, 2026-07-06.)
- **Citation.** 3.5.2 / 3.5.1.2 ("shift", directionless). No-op shifts are not
  enumerated (left at box 0, right at the off-right position).
- **Encoded in.** `actions.enumerate_call_to_arms` (left/right variants for
  `cta_loot` and the Empress shift_cylinder effect; handlers already accepted
  `direction`); tests `test_decisions_d002m_d003.py::test_cta_loot_shifts_right_352`
  / `test_cta_empress_shifts_right_3512`.


## D-008 (from Q-004, 2026-07-05) — Sally resolves on the per-Lord Battle machinery

- **Question.** S3 Betrayal / S6 Command Confusion / R24 Cavalry Charge are
  Battle holds and a Sally is a Battle (4.9.2), but their per-Lord ordering
  effects had no exact home in the side-aggregate Sally resolver. Approximate,
  leave them Sally-ineligible, or rework the Sally engine?
- **Decision.** "Unfortunately, I think the invasive thing to do is the correct
  thing to do." (Eric, 2026-07-06.) Rework the Sally onto resolve_battle's
  per-Lord machinery so every Battle hold plays exactly.
- **Citation.** 4.5.3/4.9.2 ("Attack Besiegers in a Battle"; Battle rules with
  the 4.9.2 exceptions: Besiegers' Siegeworks as Walls vs Sallying strikes
  only, no Walls/Garrison for the Sallying side, Raid on a failed Sally,
  Siege ends if the Besiegers lose).
- **Encoded in.** Commit ce39ae6: `battle.resolve_sally` on `_strike_phase`
  (new `sally_walls`) + `_end_battle` (new `withdraw_inside`); full
  `_BATTLE_HOLDS` set in `h_cmd_sally`; tests `test_decisions_d008_sally.py`,
  `test_sally_concede.py` (rebaselined).


## D-009 (from Q-005, 2026-07-05) — Bounty Cart allowance is PER-LORD (errata text governs)

- **Question.** Errata Bounty: "1 VP per Loot ... up to the number of Carts he
  and co-located Lords currently possess" — per-Lord cap, or a shared
  per-Locale pool as the Playbook Winter example computes (2 returned, not 3)?
- **Decision.** "The errata should trump." (Eric, 2026-07-06.) Per-Lord cap:
  each qualifying Lord returns up to the GROUP's Carts. The Playbook example's
  shared-pool arithmetic is superseded by the errata sentence.
- **Citation.** Errata & Clarifications Jan-2026, 4.7.6 Bounty (authority rank
  1); Playbook is examples-only (rank 4).
- **Encoded in.** No code change — `campaign._bounty` already implements the
  per-Lord cap. This entry pins it as adjudicated, not accidental.

# Seljuk Harness — LLM Play Guide

This guide lets another agent (or person) play a full game of GMT's *Seljuk*
through the harness. The harness implements the rules and auto-resolves dice; you supply the
decisions. Published rules, errata, and recorded adjudications remain the
authority, and tests do not establish that every reachable position is bug-free.

For token-efficient sandbox play, use `scripts/chatgpt_play_helper.py`; see
`CHATGPT_PLAY.md` for compact overviews, complete action pages, versioned ids,
private response handoffs, intact references, and explicit Plans. The guide
below describes the legacy, trusted `seljuk.cli` interface against a
**save file** (a JSON game state). Every command reads that file; `do` also
writes it back. Run commands with:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m seljuk.cli <command> [args]
```

(If the package is installed, just `seljuk <command>`.)

## Scenarios

`emperor_and_the_lion`, `specter_of_norman_betrayal`, `year_of_treacherous_ambition`,
`showdown_in_anatolia`, `manzikert`. The two sides are **seljuk** and **roman**.

## The turn loop

The whole game is this loop. Repeat until the game is over.

```bash
# 1. Start a game (once)
python -m seljuk.cli new emperor_and_the_lion --seed 1 --out game.json

# 2. Read the situation (human-readable). Note the DECISION owner (which may differ from the active side).
python -m seljuk.cli briefing --file game.json

# 3. Resolve any owed sub-decisions FIRST (see "Pending" below).
python -m seljuk.cli pending --file game.json

# 4. List the decision owner's legal actions (machine-readable JSON palette).
python -m seljuk.cli legal-moves --file game.json

# 5. Pick ONE action and apply it. This saves the new state back to the file.
python -m seljuk.cli do --file game.json --action '{"type": "pass_step"}'

# 6. Go back to step 2.
```

Each command prints a status line like
`phase=campaign/campaign.command  active=seljuk  actions_left=3  box=4/12`
so you always know whose turn it is and where you are. When the game ends it
prints `GAME OVER - winner: seljuk|roman|draw`.

### Choosing an action

`legal-moves` returns a JSON array of action objects. Each has a `type` and the
parameters the handler needs, plus a human `_desc`. To play one, pass it to
`do`. You may keep or drop the `_`-prefixed hint fields — the engine ignores
them. Example:

```bash
python -m seljuk.cli do --file game.json \
  --action '{"type": "cmd_march", "lord": "alp_arslan", "to": "ani", "way_type": "road"}'
```

### Validated palette (optional, recommended for agents)

`legal-moves --validate` returns the same palette but first probes every concrete
candidate on a throwaway copy of the game and **drops any move the rules engine
would reject**, printing each drop as an over-enumeration diagnostic on stderr.
So an agent that plays only from the validated palette never submits an illegal
move. (Templated moves — `build_plan`, `resolve_event`, `respond_approach`,
`assign_themata_defenders` — can't be probed blind and are returned marked
`"_unvalidated": true`.) It is slower (a probe per candidate) so it is for the
interactive/agent path, not bulk sweeps.

If you submit an illegal action, `do` prints `IllegalAction: <reason>` and exits
non-zero **without changing the game** — pick a different move. Concrete validated rows are probed in the current state; templates and added
parameter combinations still require validation. A stale state can change legality.

### Template actions and optional parameters

Most moves are ready to apply as-is. Some are templates or carry optional
parameters (hinted by `_`-prefixed keys):

- **build_plan** (Campaign Plan step). `legal-moves` gives `_plan_size` (how many
  cards), `_available_lords`, and `_treachery_required`. Build an ordered list
  of that many entries, each a Lord id (whose Command card you play, ≤4 per
  Lord), `"no_command"` (use `_constraints.no_command_max`, normally five,
  six when Treachery adds the extra card), or `"treachery"` (exactly one, only if
  `_treachery_required`). `_no_command_required` includes Treachery and Weather;
  `_constraints` exposes the engine's exact requirements. Example:
  ```bash
  --action '{"type":"build_plan","side":"seljuk","cards":["alp_arslan","alp_arslan","afsin_beg","no_command","no_command","no_command","no_command"]}'
  ```
- **cmd_march with a Group March** (4.3.1). A `cmd_march` move that carries a
  `_co_marchers` hint (a list of co-located friendly Lord ids) and `_co_marcher_max`
  may optionally bring some of those Lords. Add a `"group"` list (a subset of
  `_co_marchers`, at most `_co_marcher_max`) to March them together:
  ```bash
  --action '{"type":"cmd_march","lord":"alp_arslan","to":"ararat","way_type":"pass","group":["arisighi"]}'
  ```
  The active Lord leads (he must be a Commander, or an S7 Trusted Commander who
  may bring exactly one). The whole group moves to the destination and the action
  cost is recomputed for the combined (possibly Laden) group, so a Group March may
  cost more than the solo March shown. Omit `group` to March alone.
- **cmd_march discard variants** (1.7.2). A Laden group's March move may carry
  `discard_excess` (over-laden: shed the excess Provender just to move) and/or a
  separate `discard_to_unladen` variant (shed all Loot + excess Provender to March
  one Command action cheaper). Apply whichever the menu offers; both shed Assets,
  so they are offered as explicit alternatives to the full-cost Laden March.
- **cmd_siege variants** (4.5.1). Besides the default Siege (roll Surrender, then
  add Siegeworks on failure), the menu may offer `roll_surrender:false` (add a
  Siegeworks without rolling) and, with R25 held, `honors_of_war:true` (a Fort
  auto-Surrenders). Pick the variant object as offered.
- **build_plan lieutenants** (4.1.3). The build_plan move hints
  `_lieutenant_options` (eligible `{"lieutenant": L, "lower_lord": M}` pairs:
  same side, co-located, neither a Commander, neither already stacked). Pass a
  `"lieutenants"` list of such pairs to appoint them for the Campaign; the
  Lieutenant then plays his Lower Lord's Command cards.
- **In-Battle Held Events** (`battle_events`). Moves that start a combat accept
  `"battle_events": {"seljuk": [...], "roman": [...]}` naming Held Event cards
  EITHER side plays for that combat. Player-facing palettes expose only the
  viewing player's hand, via `_combat_inputs`. A trusted CLI caller collects
  both players' choices; the compact helper supplies explicit private handoffs. Battle (Stand/Sortie) AND Sally
  (D-008) honor the full set R2/S2/S3/S6/R24/R21/S21 (S6/R24 entries are
  dicts naming the Roman Lord: `{"card":"R24","lord":...}`); Storm honors
  R21/S21 plus, for the Roman defender, `"play_sultans_horse": true`
  (R4: Rounds -1, disclosed only to the Roman player).
- **steeled_rounds** (R3 Steeled Resolve). Any combat-starting move accepts
  `"steeled_rounds": {LORD: N}` — the Round (default 1) in which that Lord's
  Capability applies.
- **local_scouts** (R18, respond_approach). The Roman Approaching player declares
  R18; the avoiding side selects the Lord and Stand/Withdraw. A trusted CLI
  caller collects that response as `"local_scouts": {"lord": L, "action": "stand"}`.
  The compact helper separates the declaration and the enemy's selection.
- **besiege_bypass with surprise** (S1). The menu offers a
  `{"choice":"besiege","surprise":true}` variant when S1 is held and eligible;
  optionally add `storm_decisions` for the immediate Storm. If the Stronghold
  is owed a Themata assignment, that pends FIRST (S1 Clarification) and the
  2 Siege markers + Storm resume after it.
- **Loyalty coin DRMs** (1.4.1). `resolve_loyalty` / `discard_imperial_coffers`
  accept `"coins_for"` (revealing player, +1 each) and `"coins_against"` (that
  player's opponent, -1 each), bounded by the `_max_coins_for` /
  `_max_coins_against` hints (Commander + co-located Unbesieged Lords' Coin;
  no resisting for a Besieged target). The opponent pays even when the target
  already belongs to the revealing player. Amounts must be nonnegative JSON
  integers: strings, fractions, booleans, and negative values are rejected.
  Both payments are validated before any Coin or dice are consumed. Invalid
  Imperial Coffers payments also leave its card and pending decision intact.
- **resolve_event** (an immediate Arts-of-War Event that needs a choice). Pass
  `args` with the choice the card calls for, e.g.
  `{"type":"resolve_event","card":"R5","args":{"lord":"alp_arslan","direction":"left"}}`.
  Look the card up with `lookup_card` semantics (its text is in
  `data/static/cards.json`). Events that need no choice resolve with `args:{}`.

## Pending sub-decisions

After some actions the game owes a sub-decision before normal play resumes.
`pending` lists them; resolve each with `do`. The mapping:

| pending `type` | resolve with action |
|----------------|---------------------|
| `deploy_capability` | `{"type":"deploy_capability","card":C,"lord":L}` (L from `eligible`) |
| `event_pending_resolution` | `{"type":"resolve_event","card":C,"args":{...}}` |
| `approach_response` | `{"type":"respond_approach","choices":{LORD:{"action":"stand"\|"withdraw"\|"avoid","to":LOCALE}}}` |
| `besiege_or_bypass` | `{"type":"besiege_bypass","choice":"besiege"\|"bypass"}` |
| `assign_themata_defenders` | `{"type":"assign_themata_defenders","markers":[...]}` |
| `ravage_defence` | `{"type":"resolve_ravage_defence","defend_with":INDEX_or_null}` |
| `loyalty_check` | `{"type":"resolve_loyalty","target":LORD}` (from `targets`; optional `coins_for`/`coins_against`, see hints) |
| `basil_response` | `{"type":"basil_response","play":true\|false}` |
| `retain_themata` | `{"type":"retain_themata","lord":L,"thema":THEMA,"mode":"pay"}`; or `"return"`, or `"pressed_levy"` when offered (4.7.5/R4) |
| `winter_quarters` | `{"type":"winter_quarters","lord":L,"dest":SEAT}` or `{"lord":L,"stay":true}` (R15/S15; options in the pending's `dests`/`may_stay`) |

Battles, Storms, and Sallies are **auto-resolved** by the engine when you Stand
(or Storm/Sally); the result is returned by `do`. You don't roll dice — the
seeded RNG in the save file does, deterministically. Typed `battle_decisions`
(and `storm_decisions`) accept JSON arrays, for example `[["concede", true]]`.
Tuple-valued choices use a nested array, such as
`[["retreat", ["retreat", "ani"]]]`, subject to the offered destinations.

S11 Javelins fires in one Battle round per Battle, not every round and not in
Storm. Supply `"javelins_rounds": {"ibn_khan": 2}` on `respond_approach`,
`cmd_sortie`, or `cmd_sally` to mark round 2 for that Lord. The default is round 1.
The same syntax applies to `steeled_rounds` for R3 Steeled Resolve.

At a non-final Campaign Reset, the Roman player may retain all of a Thema's
Levied/Recruited units on a Lord's mat for **one Coin per Thema**, not per unit or
marker. Resolve each `retain_themata` pending before continuing. `pressed_levy`
is offered for R4's one free unpaid Thema; `return` declines retention. The save
file preserves these choices, including a partially completed Reset.

Themata `symbols` are the printed marker capacity. On a Lord's mat, optional
`strength` records surviving units and `routed` records its routed subset; a
missing/null strength means full printed strength. Human Lord/summary views
include the surviving Themata in Forces while displaying their marker identity.
Older saves without these fields remain loadable.

## Hidden information

`state --file game.json --side seljuk --json` returns the machine-readable game
state **filtered for that side**: the opponent's draw deck, held Events, and
unrevealed Plan cards are masked as `"<hidden>"`. Your own are fully visible, as
are the opponent's already-revealed Command cards. The filtered view exposes
only action types from replay history and omits the random seed/state; raw
history includes secret plans and is not a player-safe event log. Human and JSON state/briefing views default to the decision owner and honor
Hidden Mats. `history --raw`, raw save files, and direct render APIs without a
viewing side remain trusted omniscient debugging access.

## Winning

`is_over` is true when `phase == game_over`; the winner is in the status line and
in `winner`. Victory comes from VP (½ per Ruins/Ravaged, 1 per Roman-Conquered),
the Seljuk Unity track, or an Aleppo auto-victory — all scored by the engine.

## Mode A — Solo / single chat

One chat drives both sides (or plays one side and makes reasonable moves for the
other). Just run the turn loop; the `decision` side in the status line tells you
who owes the next input (not necessarily the active Command-card player). Nothing else to coordinate.

## Mode B — Head-to-head (two chats)

Two chats play a real game, one as **seljuk** and one as **roman**, sharing a
single save file in a folder both can read/write (e.g. the Cowork workspace).

Setup (either chat, once):
```bash
python -m seljuk.cli new <scenario> --out /path/to/shared/game.json
```

Each chat's turn protocol:
1. `briefing --file game.json` and read the status line. **Act only when
   `decision=` is your side.** The inactive defender can owe an immediate response.
2. View your own state: `state --file game.json --side YOUR_SIDE --json`.
3. Resolve `pending` decisions that are yours, then `legal-moves`, then `do`.
4. After your `do`, the status line shows whose turn is next. Hand off (the file
   is already saved).

Honor system: the harness does **not** stop a chat from reading the opponent's
filtered-out info or applying the opponent's moves. For a fair game, each chat
should only ever call `state --side ITS_OWN_SIDE`, only resolve pending
decisions owed by its side, and only `do` actions for its own Lords. The
`legal-moves` palette follows the actual decision owner. Do not send an
actor's private `do` result to the next decision owner. For enforced presentation
pins and staged joint decisions use the compact helper; the CLI is a trusted
low-level interface, not an authentication boundary.

For fair head-to-head play, keep private action results private: they can
contain a Plan or other hidden choices. `history` and unfiltered save files are
omniscient debugging/replay tools, not public turn logs. Use your side-filtered
state to review public information.

## Longest-scenario corrections (2026-10-10)

After an Approach Battle, resolve any `besiege_or_bypass` decision and subsequent
`assign_themata_defenders` decision before recovery. This applies in Winter as
well as normal Campaigns. Battle leaves no further Command actions, including
when Bypass is selected; `end_activation` cannot skip the mandatory decision.

The `build_plan` hint `_no_command_required` covers both Treachery's compulsory
opponent No Command and Unpredictable Weather. Supply at least one `no_command`
when it is true, within the displayed `_plan_size`.

This-Campaign cards return to their decks at Reset. S13 Peace Offering becomes
Gifts Exchanged in the Capability area; its Event effect is tracked by the
seasonal flag, not a second physical card in `this_campaign_events`.
